text:
anya: heads-up — customer (acct redacted) opened a ticket: repeated 504s and intermittent 5xx from hosted /v1/generate around 18:04 UTC. They say p95 timeouts on long-seq prompts, small overall qps (~30 rps) but spikes tied to some long-running jobs. attaching support ticket logs.

mike: thanks. any shard/tenant id in the logs? can you paste an example request id? :eyes:

anya: sample request id: req_b2c9f2. payload is ~12k tokens, streaming enabled. customer says partial stream then hangs. attached curl they used:

support-bot: ```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"model":"open-llm-xl","input":"<long prompt>","stream":true}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

opsbot: alert: gateway-error-rate spike for tenant-2234 at 2026-03-17T18:04: queue_depth=198/200, inflight_longseq=24, continuous_batch_backlog=63, kvcache_miss_rate=0.78

mike: that queue_depth is basically at the per-tenant limit. 198/200 will start early reject/fallbacks. looks like long sequences are occupying many batch slots (kv cache heatup). can we surface any stack traces or internal 5xx codes?

anya: pasted last 5xx from gateway:

support-bot: ```
[2026-03-17T18:06:21Z] req=req_b2c9f2 tenant=2234 status=502 upstream_error="batcher-timeout" details="batcher blocked waiting for kv cache" p95=12.1s
[2026-03-17T18:06:22Z] req=req_b2c9f2 tenant=2234 status=504 details="request-deadline"
```

sre-oncall: oncall here — taking this. initial hypothesis: continuous batching backlog + kvcache cold misses causing long wait times per batch, leading to queue saturation and deadline timeouts. low qps overall but longseqs can occupy many slots and stall the batcher.

mike: agreed. steps to repro locally? need to simulate longseqs hitting same shard and kvcache misses.

sre-oncall: repro plan quick:
- spawn 6 parallel clients sending ~12k-token prompts with streaming enabled
- pin to model=open-llm-xl and to the hosted gateway region (us-east)
- monitor /metrics: request_queue_depth, continuous_batch_backlog, kvcache_miss_rate, batcher_wait_ms

opsbot: metric snapshot (18:05 UTC): request_queue_depth=195, continuous_batch_backlog=58, batcher_wait_ms=4200, kvcache_miss_rate=0.77, host_cpu=62%

anya: tried a quick mitigation: increased tenant queue limit to 400 for tenant-2234 and toggled short-circuit caching for their requests. told customer to retry.

mike: what happened after increase?

sre-oncall: after limit increase and enabling aggressive prefix caching for that tenant, backlog dropped to ~12 within 90s, p95 improved to ~1.1s, no new 504s. but that's a stopgap.

eve-csm: customer accepted the temporary change but asked for long-term fix — they run a scheduled batch of long-generation jobs every day.

mike: permanent mitigations we should discuss:
1) per-tenant longseq throttling / token-based admission control
2) tune continuous-batcher to prefer shorter sequences when backlog grows (avoid head-of-line blocking)
3) better kvcache warmup for known tenant model variants (prepopulate on schedule)
4) circuit breaker that rejects excessive inflight longseqs with clear 429 + retry-after instead of letting queue saturate

sre-oncall: agreed. I'll open an RFC for (1) and (4). engineering quick fixes: expose a tenant config for max_inflight_tokens and a scheduler to prewarm kv for customers with predictable long jobs.

anya: created support ticket update and notified customer of the temporary change + next steps. they want ETA for RFC.

sre-oncall: will target a proposal EOD tomorrow. quick patch to batcher to reduce wait_ms threshold for building big batches is low-risk, I'll push a canary to staging later today.

mike: please add runbook steps to detect this pattern automatically: alert when kvcache_miss_rate > 0.5 AND continuous_batch_backlog > 40 for >2mins.

opsbot: noted. created alert rule draft: alert:TenantLongseqSpillover -> triggers on combined signal above.

anya: thanks team. any other asks from CS?

eve-csm: customer requested we throttle their scheduled job to run off-peak; I sent a workflow template to their SREs. :thumbsup:

mike: great. follow-ups: (a) RFC for tenant admission controls, (b) canary batcher patch, (c) alert + runbook updates, (d) prewarm plan for high-volume longseq tenants. I'll triage owners in jira.

sre-oncall: I'll post link to canary and repro steps once ready. closing this Slack thread for now, will update when RFC is posted. :white_check_mark:
